synthesized via arc-melting high-purity (≥ 99.95 wt%) Ti, Al, Cr, Fe, and Ni elemental metals under an argon atmosphere. To ensure thorough mixing and compositional uniformity, each ingot was flipped and remelted at least five times on a copper mold.
Subsequently, the ingots were drop-cast into a copper mold under an argon atmosphere to produce slabs with dimensions of 50 × 12 × 2 mm3
These slabs were sealed in quartz tubes with argon and homogenized at 1373 K for 5 h, followed by water quenching.
After homogenization, the slabs were surface-polished and cold-rolled to reduce their thickness by 50 %, achieving a final thickness of approximately 1 mm.
